title: Long and Short: hosszú / rövid, and próbál

sections.content: hosszú ('long') and rövid ('short') are another common opposite pair for describing clothes. próbál ('to try') is a regular verb: próbálok ('I try'), and combines with fel- to give felpróbál ('to try on').
Hungarian treats 'nadrág' (trousers) as a single, singular noun, so the adjective stays singular too: 'a nadrág hosszú', not a plural form -- unlike English 'the trousers ARE long'.
